title: incident-artifact-retention-and-rotation-orchestration-guide
author: Samira Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This guide defines the company standard for incident artifacts (logs, traces, KV cache snapshots, model checkpoints, request/response payloads), how long each artifact class is retained, where artifacts are stored and indexed, and the orchestration patterns we use to rotate on-call duties and hand off artifact custody during incidents. The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence for post-incident analysis, satisfy regulatory requirements, and minimize storage cost while preserving forensics fidelity.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production incidents affecting Redwood-hosted inference, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments where Redwood collects telemetry.
- Covers artifact classification, automated collection, retention schedules, secure storage and access controls, rotation/handover procedures for on-call personnel, game-day scenarios, and templates for customer-facing status and postmortems.

Definitions
-----------
- Artifact: any persisted data collected to investigate an incident (logs, traces, span dumps, KV cache dumps, model-run transcripts, input/outputs).
- Artifact Custodian: the on-call engineer or rotation team responsible for ensuring artifacts are collected, retained, and shared per policy during the incident lifecycle.
- Short TTL Incident: SLO/glitch events with no PII exposed and limited scope (Severity 3/4).
- Long TTL Incident: Incidents with regulatory, customer contract, or forensic implications (Severity 1/2).

Retention Policy (summary table)
-------------------------------
| Artifact class | Typical retention | Encryption | Access scope | Retention trigger (auto) |
|----------------|-------------------|------------|--------------|-------------------------|
| API request+response payloads | 30 days (S3) | AES-256 | Eng + Sec (role) | Lifecycle job daily |
| Structured logs (prod) | 90 days (ELK hot,warm) | At rest & in-flight | Eng, SRE | ILM policy rollover |
| Traces/spans | 45 days | AES-256 | Eng, Observability | Aggregation -> snapshot TTL |
| KV cache dumps (model runtime) | 14 days (encrypted blobstore) | Customer-specific & AES-256 | Runtime team, customer SLA | Retain if severity>=2 or customer-requested |
| Model run transcripts (text outputs) | 30 days default; 365 days if regulatory flagged | Redacted by default | Eng, Product, Legal (if needed) | Archive job on incident close |
| Full model checkpoints or state | 365 days (restricted) | HSM/KMS | Research + Ops only | Manual retention request with approval |
| Forensic snapshots (disk images/container states) | 7 years or per legal hold | Air-gapped encrypted storage | Legal, Security, Exec | Manual legal hold only |

Policy details and rationale
---------------------------
- Default retention durations are cost/forensics tradeoffs decided by Product, Security, and Finance. Shorter TTLs keep storage cheap; longer retention requires approval and documented business case.
- All artifacts containing potential PII or customer-provided data MUST be redacted at collection time where possible. If redaction is impossible, mark artifact with confidentiality metadata and escalate to Security.
- Artifact collection is automated for the top-20% of alert signatures by volume. For lower-volume signatures, the responding engineer must trigger collection using the runbook commands below.

Automated collection and indexing
--------------------------------
- Collector service: redwood-artifact-collector (internal service). It subscribes to alert topics and to runtime signals.
- Index: elastic-artifacts (index mapping includes incident_id, service, region, severity, tags, custody).
- Collection flow (automated):
  1. Alert triggers collector with incident_id.
  2. Collector runs ephemeral agents to snapshot logs/traces and stores artifacts to encrypted S3 with object metadata.
  3. Collector posts artifact index entries to elastic-artifacts and notifies the incident bridge channel with a summary.

Rotation orchestration (how we schedule and hand off on-call)
--------------------------------------------------------------
Principles:
- Clear custody: the engineer currently on primary on-call is the Artifact Custodian for an active incident until custody is explicitly handed off.
- Minimum cognitive load: handover tasks are checklist-based and automated where possible.
- Auditability: every custody handoff must be recorded in the incident timeline with timestamp, from and to, reason.

Rotation automation components
- rotator-service: schedules rotations and writes calendar invites for primary/secondary.
- handoff-bot (Slack): invokes /handoff incident_id @new_primary and records a custody event.
- custody-tagging: artifacts include a custody metadata key (custodian:email).

Handover checklist (to be completed in the incident bridge)
1) Post current incident summary in bridge channel: impact, SLOs affected, current mitigation attempts.
2) Confirm artifacts collected: list object keys for logs, traces, KV dumps.
3) Run quick integrity check: md5sum of saved blobs vs collector log.
4) Annotate artifact index: add tags for severity and regulatory_flags.
5) Run access grant automation (if new custodian needs elevated access) with temporary 2-hour role.
6) Invoke /handoff and confirm acceptance by new custodian.
7) New custodian posts acknowledgement and next steps.

Runbook: Artifact collection for degraded-latency incidents (Severity 2/3)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: capture enough context to reconstruct request flow and KV cache state for root cause analysis.
Preconditions: access to incident_id and bridge channel.
Steps:
1. Trigger automated collector (preferred):
   - CLI: redwoodctl incident collect-artifacts --id INCIDENT-12345 --scope latency
   - Expected output: "collection-OK -> s3://redwood-artifacts/incident-12345/collection-20260203T1432.gz"
2. If automated fails, run manual commands on the runtime node:
   - ssh runtime-01
   - sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime --since "2026-02-03 13:00" | gzip -9 > /tmp/serving-runtime-journal.gz
   - sudo /opt/redwood/bin/dump-kvcache --model-id=model-abc --out /tmp/kv-dump-INC12345.bin
   - Encrypt blobs: gpg --encrypt --recipient "artifact-ingest@redwood.ai" /tmp/*INC12345*
   - Upload: aws s3 cp /tmp/serving-runtime-journal.gz s3://redwood-artifacts/incident-12345/ --server-side-encryption AES256
3. Post the object keys into the incident timeline and tag them as custody=primary.
4. If model transcripts are sensitive, run redwoodctl redact --input s3://... --policy transcript-default and then re-index.

Game day scenario: "KV-eviction cascade"
--------------------------------------
Objective: validate artifact collection, custody handoff, and rotation bot integration under a simulated severe degradation.
Preparatory steps (3 days before):
- Notify rotation participants and create calendar event with playbook link.
- Ensure redwood-artifact-collector test mode has adequate quota.
Execution script (during drill):
1) Trigger synthetic incident: curl -X POST https://ops-api/internal/fake-incident -d '{"scenario":"kv-eviction","severity":2}'
2) Observe collector behavior and confirm artifacts appear in the incident index within 60s.
3) Conduct a handoff at 15 minutes into the drill and verify custody metadata updated and handoff event recorded.
4) Run post-drill checklist: export retention metrics (size, object counts), confirm TTL lifecycle jobs executed, collect participant feedback.
Success criteria:
- Artifacts indexed within 60s of trigger,
- Handoff recorded and visible in timeline,
- No unredacted transcripts left in public indexes.

Status page and customer comms templates
---------------------------------------
Public status page (short template):
- Title: Service degradation for Redwood API (region-us-west-2)
- Summary: We are experiencing elevated latency for text-generation requests in us-west-2. Engineers are investigating and restoring capacity.
- Impact: Some API requests may take >2s to complete or may return 503 when retries exhausted.
- ETA: Next update in 30 minutes.
- Mitigation: Retries and fallback to model-variant 'gptlite-v1' are in effect for domestic customers.
- Link to details: [internal-incident-INC-12345]

Customer-facing email (stakeholder template)
Subject: Incident INC-12345 — Elevated latency impacting text-generation (us-west-2)\Body:
Hello <Customer Name>,

We detected elevated latency for text-generation calls served from us-west-2 beginning 2026-02-03 13:20 UTC. Our engineers identified a KV cache eviction cascade under high traffic and initiated mitigations (auto-scaling and model fallbacks) at 13:34 UTC. We are continuing restoration and will follow up with a detailed incident report within 48 hours.

What we collected: logs, traces, and a KV cache snapshot stored under a secure, customer-scoped artifact bucket. If you would like access to your tenant-scoped artifacts for this incident, please reply and we will open a secure sharing flow per contract.

Regards,
Redwood Incident Response

Postmortem template (short)
---------------------------
- Title: [INC-12345] Short title (e.g. KV eviction cascade -> latency)
- Severity: 2
- Detection time: 2026-02-03 13:20 UTC
- Mitigation time: 2026-02-03 13:34 UTC
- Recovery time: 2026-02-03 14:05 UTC
- Summary of root cause: concise sentence
- Timeline: numbered events with times, actor, key artifacts (object keys)
- Corrective actions: short-term and long-term (owners + due dates)
- Artifact index: list of object keys for logs/traces/KV dumps and retention class
- Regulatory/contract actions: list if any legal holds or customer requests

Escalation matrix for custody or legal hold requests
--------------------------------------------------
1) On-call primary -> if legal hold suspected -> contact Security on-call (pager) and tag incident with legal_hold=true.
2) Security determines need and issues hold-token.
3) Artifact retention TTL overridden by hold-token until release.
4) Legal team notified and evidence custodian assigned.

Operational metrics and dashboards
--------------------------------
- Artifact collection success rate (target 99.5% for auto-signatures).
- Mean time to artifact indexing (target < 60s for automated flow).
- Storage churn: daily MB/day per active incident.
- Number of manual collections per month (target < 10% of incidents).

Ownership and responsibilities
------------------------------
- Artifact retention policy steward: Security (policy), Product (retention business cases), and Finance (cost approvals).
- On-call custody flow owner: Eng Platform team.
- Collector service owner: Observability team.
- Rotation scheduler owner: SRE tooling team.

Appendix A: CLI snippets
------------------------
- Trigger collector (automated):
  redwoodctl incident collect-artifacts --id INCIDENT-12345 --scope all --encrypt --notify "#incident-bridge-INC-12345"

- Request temporary access for handoff (Slack command):
  /grant-access @new_custodian --scope "artifact-read" --duration 120m --incident INCIDENT-12345

- Archive object to cold storage manually:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/incident-12345/object.gz s3://redwood-artifacts-archive/ --storage-class GLACIER

Appendix B: Quick checklist (one-pager for pocket)
--------------------------------------------------
- Did we collect logs/traces? (Y/N) -> object keys: ______
- Is KV cache dump present? (Y/N) -> object key: ______
- Is transcript redaction validated? (Y/N)
- Has custody been handed off and recorded? (Y/N)
- Was legal hold evaluated? (Y/N)

Notes and change history
------------------------
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft and approval by Eng Platform.
- 2026-01-20: Increased trace retention from 30 to 45 days after product request.
- 2026-02-03: Added encryption and temporary access automation snippets.
